_comment: When to cut supercruise overcharge, per hull. Expressed as a RANGE TO RUN, not a countdown: cut when range to target (Ls) >= a * speed(c)^p. Both numbers are on the HUD panel. A countdown does not work because braking distance grows far more slowly than speed - the observations exclude any exponent above 0.84, so the seconds-to-target needed at 2,000c is a fraction of what it is at 70c. Measured with tools/scocap.py; see tools/README.md.

fallback.note: The Panther's law, for want of a measured one. Any other hull is a guess: nothing lighter has been tested and mass is the obvious thing that would move it.

panthermkii.note: Nine captured approaches over 357 Ls and 5,394 Ls legs plus one commander report at 35,000 Ls. The boundary is pinned only near 70c, between a cut at 172 Ls that overshot and looped and a cut at 273 Ls that arrived clean. Above that speed there is no recorded overshoot, so the exponent is bounded above (0.84) but not below, and p=0.5 is a safety choice among the admissible fits: a constant distance fits equally well, the two diverge fivefold by 2,000c, and being wrong toward p=0.5 wastes seconds while being wrong toward a constant overshoots. One deliberate overshoot at high speed would settle it. Laden and empty not separated: 21 laden against 4 light arrivals showed no detectable difference, on a test that could barely detect one.
